records.source: הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ רָא֖וּ א֣וֹר גָּד֑וֹל יֹשְׁבֵי֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ צַלְמָ֔וֶת א֖וֹר נָגַ֥הּ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: The people the walking in darkness have seen light great; dwellers in [a] land of death-shadow, light has shone on them.
pieces: The people walking in the dark have seen a great light. \q Those who lived in a land as dark as death now have light shining on them.

L.1: The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light; \q those who dwell in a land of death's shadow, a light has shone on them.

R.1: The people who were living in the dark have seen a bright light. \q They lived in a land as dark as death, but now a light shines on them.

decisions.choice: Hebrew verse numbers: this is 9:1 in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text chapter 8 has twenty-three verses, and the verse about Zebulun and Naphtali and "Galilee of the nations" is 8:23. Bibles that follow the older Latin and Greek division call that verse 9:1, so 9:1-20 here are 9:2-21 there. Isaiah is cited by the Hebrew numbers throughout.

decisions.choice: death's shadow: the deepest darkness, darkness like death
decisions.reason: The word is written as if made of "shadow" and "death" (tsalmavet), and is used of the darkest places: the realm of the dead (Job 38:17), a dark valley (Psalm 23:4), a dungeon (Psalm 107:10). Whether or not it was first formed that way, it means a darkness as deep as death.

decisions.choice: have seen, has shone: the coming light is described as already here
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for completed action, following the promise of 8:23 that God will bring honor to Galilee in the time to come. A prophet can describe what God will surely do as already done. Matthew 4:15-16 quotes 8:23-9:1 of Jesus beginning his work in Galilee.

decisions.choice: a land as dark as death
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the compound (m2); Literal keeps the picture of death's shadow.

records.heading: A great light for those in the dark

records.source: הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי ל֖וֹ הִגְדַּ֣לְתָּ הַשִּׂמְחָ֑ה שָׂמְח֤וּ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ כְּשִׂמְחַ֣ת בַּקָּצִ֔יר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגִ֖ילוּ בְּחַלְּקָ֥ם שָׁלָֽל׃
records.gloss: You have multiplied the nation, to it you have made great the joy; they rejoice before you like [the] joy at the harvest, as [people] are glad when they divide plunder.
pieces: You have made the nation grow and filled it with great joy. \q In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence they are glad with the gladness of harvest time, \q the delight of those who share out the spoils of war.

L.2: You have multiplied the nation; \q for it you have made the joy great. \q They rejoice before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like the joy at harvest, \q as [people] are glad when they divide plunder.

R.2: You have made the nation large and given it great joy. \q They are happy as they stand before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, like farmers at harvest time, \q like soldiers dividing up what they took in battle.

decisions.choice: for it (the reading the scribes marked): you have made its joy great
alternatives: you have multiplied the nation, you have not increased the joy
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has "not" (lo with an aleph), which would give "you have not made the joy great". The scribes' note in the margin tells readers to say "to it", which sounds the same. "To it" fits the verse, which is all about joy, and is followed here.

decisions.choice: harvest and plunder: the two great times of rejoicing
decisions.reason: Harvest festivals and dividing the spoil after a victory were the best-known times of celebration (Psalm 4:8; Judges 5:30). The two pictures prepare for verses 3-4: the oppressor is broken and the war is over.

decisions.choice: you: God, addressed directly
decisions.reason: The prophet turns to speak to God. The nation is the people in darkness of verse 1; "before you" is the language of worship at God's sanctuary (Deuteronomy 12:7).

decisions.choice: farmers ... soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable names who rejoices at harvest and who divides plunder.

records.source: כִּ֣י׀אֶת־עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ וְאֵת֙ מַטֵּ֣ה שִׁכְמ֔וֹ שֵׁ֖בֶט הַנֹּגֵ֣שׂ בּ֑וֹ הַחִתֹּ֖תָ כְּי֥וֹם מִדְיָֽן׃
records.gloss: For the yoke of his burden and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of the [one] driving him, you have shattered as [on] the day of Midian.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have smashed the yoke that weighed them down, \q the pole pressing on their shoulders, the rod of the man who drove them, \q as on the day of Midian.

L.3: For the yoke of his burden and the staff on his shoulder, \q the rod of the one driving him, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shattered as [on] the day of Midian.

R.3: You have broken the heavy yoke they carried on their shoulders. \q You have smashed the stick of the cruel master who drove them at forced labor. \q You did it just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did on the day Gideon defeated Midian.

decisions.choice: the day of Midian: Gideon's victory (Judges 7)
decisions.reason: God gave Gideon victory over Midian with three hundred men, so that Israel could not boast that its own strength had saved it (Judges 7:2, 22). Isaiah recalls the same day in 10:26, and Psalm 83:10 asks God to act again as he did against Midian.

decisions.choice: the one driving him: the taskmaster, the oppressor
decisions.reason: The word is used of the slave drivers of Egypt (Exodus 3:7; 5:6) and of oppressive rulers (3:12; 14:2, 4). Yoke, pole and rod are the gear of forced labor.

decisions.choice: his: the people, spoken of as one
decisions.reason: "His burden" and "his shoulder" refer to the nation of verse 2, spoken of as one person. The objects are put first for weight, and the verb comes last: "you have shattered".

decisions.choice: them, their
decisions.reason: The singular collective is plural at Balanced and Readable (m3).

decisions.choice: on the day Gideon defeated Midian
decisions.reason: Readable names the event (m1).

records.source: כִּ֤י כָל־סְאוֹן֙ סֹאֵ֣ן בְּרַ֔עַשׁ וְשִׂמְלָ֖ה מְגוֹלָלָ֣ה בְדָמִ֑ים וְהָיְתָ֥ה לִשְׂרֵפָ֖ה מַאֲכֹ֥לֶת אֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: For every boot tramping with quaking, and cloak rolled in bloods, and it will be for burning, fuel of fire.
pieces: For every boot that stamped and thundered in battle, \q every cloak caked in blood, \q will go to be burned, food for the fire.

L.4: For every boot that tramped with a din \q and every cloak rolled in blood \q will be for burning, fuel for fire.

R.4: All the boots of soldiers marching to war will be burned up. \q All their clothes covered in blood will be fuel for the fire.

decisions.choice: boot ... tramping: a soldier's boot on the march
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb from it occur only here. A related word in other Semitic languages means a soldier's boot or sandal; with "shaking" or "din" it pictures an army marching.

decisions.choice: burning: the gear of war is destroyed because the war is over
decisions.reason: Burning the weapons and clothing of war means there will be no more battles. Psalm 46:10 says God makes wars cease and burns the chariots with fire, and 2:4 pictures swords beaten into plowshares.

decisions.choice: soldiers marching to war
decisions.reason: Readable says whose boots these are (m1).

records.source: כִּי־יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד־לָ֗נוּ בֵּ֚ן נִתַּן־לָ֔נוּ וַתְּהִ֥י הַמִּשְׂרָ֖ה עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִי עַ֖דשַׂר־שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: For [a] child has been born to us, [a] son has been given to us, and has come to be the dominion on his shoulder, and [one] has called his name Wonder Counselor, God Mighty, Father of Perpetuity, Prince of Peace.
pieces: For a child has been born for us, a son has been given to us, \q and the right to rule rests on his shoulders. \q He has been named Planner of Wonders, God the Mighty Warrior, \q Father for All Time, Ruler of Peace.

L.5: For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us, \q and the rule has come to be on his shoulder; \q and [one] has called his name Wonder Counselor, Mighty God, \q Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.

R.5: A child has been born for us! A son has been given to us! \q He has been given the power to rule. \q He has been named Planner of Wonders, God the Mighty Warrior, Father Forever, and Ruler Who Brings Peace.

decisions.choice: for a child has been born: the third and greatest reason for the joy
decisions.reason: Verses 3, 4 and 5 each begin with "for" and give the reasons for the joy of verse 2: the oppressor broken, the war gear burned, and now a royal child. The verbs are in the form for completed action. A prophet can speak of what God will surely do as already done, or announce a birth that has just happened; the passage does not name the child. 7:14 promised a son called Immanuel, and 11:1-5 describes a king from the line of Jesse.

decisions.choice: the rule on his shoulder: he carries the authority of the king
decisions.reason: The word for rule or dominion occurs only here and in verse 6. Authority is pictured as something carried on the shoulder, as the key of David's house is laid on Eliakim's shoulder in 22:22. This is the opposite of the yoke on the people's shoulder in verse 3.

decisions.choice: one has called his name: he is given these names, the namer unstated
decisions.reason: The verb is active, "and he called", with no subject named. It may be impersonal ("his name is called"), which is how the Septuagint takes it, or God may be the one who gives the names. Either way, these are the names the child bears.

decisions.choice: four titles of the child, each made of two words
alternatives: one sentence-name about God: "The mighty God plans wonders; the eternal Father is a ruler of peace"
decisions.reason: Isaiah's own sons have names that are sentences about God's acts (Shear-jashub in 7:3; Maher-shalal-hash-baz in 8:3), and Immanuel means "God is with us" (7:14; 8:8). Read that way, these words could be one long name that speaks about God and not about the child: "a planner of wonders is the mighty God; the everlasting father is a prince of peace". But they stand after "his name" as four pairs, each a title, and verse 6 goes straight on to describe this king's rule on David's throne. They are taken here as titles of the child himself.

decisions.choice: Planner of Wonders: a counselor whose plans are wonders
decisions.reason: The first word is the noun "a wonder", used of the extraordinary acts only God does (Exodus 15:11; 25:1; 29:14). The second is "one who counsels, who plans", a role of kings (Micah 4:9). In 28:29 the same two roots describe the LORD of hosts, who makes his counsel wonderful. The title is more than "a good adviser": his plans are wonders.

decisions.choice: Mighty God: God the mighty warrior
decisions.reason: The first word is the common short word for God; the second means a mighty man, a warrior, a hero. In 10:21 the same two words name the God to whom the remnant of Jacob will return, and Deuteronomy 10:17 and Jeremiah 32:18 call God "the great, the mighty". The plural of the first word can mean "mighty ones", that is, chiefs (Ezekiel 32:21), so the pair could mean "mighty hero"; but in Isaiah the singular always means God or a god (31:3; 44:15). Read as a title of the child, it gives a king the name of God, as Psalm 45:7 addresses the king's throne as God's.

decisions.choice: Father Forever: one who is a father to his people for all time
decisions.reason: "Father" is used of a ruler who protects and provides for his people: Eliakim will be "a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem" (22:21). The second word means lasting time, perpetuity, as in "forever" in verse 6 and in 26:4; 57:15 says God inhabits it.

decisions.choice: Prince of Peace: a ruler whose reign brings peace
decisions.reason: The first word is used of princes, officials and commanders (1:23; 3:3; 32:1). Verse 6 explains the title: peace without end. Peace here is safety and well-being for the whole kingdom, after the war gear of verse 4 is burned.

decisions.choice: Planner of Wonders, God the Mighty Warrior, Father for All Time (Forever), Ruler of Peace (Who Brings Peace)
alternatives: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the shortest form of each pair. Balanced and Readable say what each title means (m5-m8), instead of the familiar "Wonderful Counselor", "Everlasting Father" and "Prince of Peace".

decisions.choice: He has been named
decisions.reason: The active verb with no subject (m3) is put in the passive at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "[one] has called".

records.source: לְמַרְבֵּ֨ההַמִּשְׂרָ֜ה וּלְשָׁל֣וֹם אֵֽין־קֵ֗ץ עַל־כִּסֵּ֤א דָוִד֙ וְעַל־מַמְלַכְתּ֔וֹ לְהָכִ֤ין אֹתָהּ֙ וּֽלְסַעֲדָ֔הּ בְּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּבִצְדָקָ֑ה מֵעַתָּה֙ וְעַד־עוֹלָ֔ם קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־זֹּֽאת׃ס
records.gloss: Of [the] increase of the dominion and of peace [there is] no end, on [the] throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from now and until forever. [The] zeal of Yahweh of hosts will do this.
pieces: His rule will grow and grow, and its peace will never end, on David's throne and over his kingdom, \q as he makes it firm and holds it up with justice and righteousness \q from now on and for all time. \q The burning zeal of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will make this happen.

L.6: Of the increase of the rule and of peace there [will be] no end, on the throne of David and over his kingdom, \q to establish it and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness \q from now and until forever. \q The zeal of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will do this.

R.6: His power to rule will keep growing, and there will be peace without end. \q He will rule as king on David's throne and over David's kingdom. \q He will make the kingdom strong and keep it standing by doing what is fair and right, from now on and forever. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart on doing this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it.

decisions.choice: of the increase: one word, as the scribes read it
alternatives: to them, great will be the rule
decisions.reason: In the Leningrad Codex the word for "increase" is written with the closed form of the letter mem that belongs at the end of a word, as if it were two words ("to them" and "great"). The scribes' note reads it as one word with the ordinary letter, and the sense "of the increase" fits the verse. The odd letter is a well-known peculiarity of this verse.

decisions.choice: the throne of David and his kingdom: the promise to David
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose throne and kingdom he would establish forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Psalm 89:4-5, 30). The same verb "establish" is used there. Luke 1:32-33 echoes this verse: the throne of David and a kingdom with no end.

decisions.choice: zeal: God's burning commitment
decisions.reason: The word means intense, passionate devotion; when someone or something rivals what is God's own it is "jealousy" (Exodus 20:5). Here it is God's determination to keep his promise. The same sentence closes the promise of a remnant in 37:32.

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness: rule that is fair and right
decisions.reason: The pair describes what God looked for in Israel and did not find (5:7) and the king of 11:4-5 and 32:1.

decisions.choice: has set his heart on doing this
decisions.reason: Readable explains "zeal" (m3).

records.source: דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְנָפַ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: [A] word has sent [the] Lord against Jacob, and it has fallen on Israel.
pieces: The Lord has sent out a word against Jacob, \q and it has come down on Israel.

L.7: A word the Lord has sent against Jacob, \q and it has fallen on Israel.

R.7: The Lord has sent a message against the people of Jacob. \q It has come down on the kingdom of Israel.

decisions.choice: a word ... has fallen: God's spoken judgment, sent like a weapon
decisions.reason: God's word is not only a message but a power that does what it says (55:10-11). It is "sent" and "falls" like a blow. This begins a poem in four stanzas, each ending with the same refrain (9:11, 16, 20; 10:4).

decisions.choice: Jacob, Israel: the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Verse 8 names Ephraim and Samaria, the northern kingdom and its capital. Jacob and Israel here are the ten northern tribes, not Judah.

decisions.choice: the people of Jacob, the kingdom of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear the names stand for a people and a kingdom (m2).

records.heading: A word sent against Jacob

records.source: וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן בְּגַאֲוָ֛ה וּבְגֹ֥דֶל לֵבָ֖ב לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And will know the people, all of it, Ephraim and [the] inhabitant of Samaria, in pride and in greatness of heart, saying,
pieces: Every one of them will find it out, \q Ephraim and everyone living in Samaria, \q the people who boast with proud, swollen hearts,

L.8: And the people will know, all of them, \q Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, \q who say in pride and in greatness of heart,

R.8: All the people of Ephraim and of the city of Samaria will learn what it means. \q They are proud and think they are great. They say,

decisions.choice: Ephraim and Samaria: the northern kingdom and its capital
decisions.reason: Ephraim was the leading tribe of the north, and its name stands for the whole kingdom (7:2, 5, 8-9). Samaria was its capital city, built by Omri (1 Kings 16:24).

decisions.choice: will know: will learn by experience
decisions.reason: To know here is to feel the force of God's word, to find out what it means by what happens to them.

decisions.choice: greatness of heart: arrogance
decisions.reason: A big or swollen heart is pride. The same phrase is used of the king of Assyria in 10:12.

records.source: לְבֵנִ֥ים נָפָ֖לוּ וְגָזִ֣ית נִבְנֶ֑ה שִׁקְמִ֣ים גֻּדָּ֔עוּ וַאֲרָזִ֖ים נַחֲלִֽיף׃
records.gloss: Bricks have fallen, and [with] hewn [stone] we will build; sycamores have been cut down, and cedars we will put in place.
pieces: "Brick has tumbled down, but we will build in cut stone; \q sycamore wood has been chopped down, \q but cedar will take its place."

L.9: "Bricks have fallen, but [with] dressed stone we will build; \q sycamores have been cut down, \q but cedars we will put in [their] place."

R.9: "Our brick walls have fallen, but we will build again with fine cut stone. \q The common sycamore trees have been cut down, but we will use costly cedar in their place."

decisions.choice: brick and sycamore, cut stone and cedar: cheap materials and costly ones
decisions.reason: Sun-dried brick and sycamore-fig timber were the ordinary building materials; dressed stone and cedar were for palaces and the temple. Solomon made cedar as common as the sycamores (1 Kings 10:27).

decisions.choice: the boast: refusing to see the disaster as God's warning
decisions.reason: The people treat the damage as a chance to build something better. Verse 12 shows what they failed to do: turn back to the one who struck them.

decisions.choice: common ... costly
decisions.reason: Readable says why the materials are named (m1).

records.source: וַיְשַׂגֵּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־צָרֵ֥י רְצִ֖ין עָלָ֑יו וְאֶת־אֹיְבָ֖יו יְסַכְסֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And raised high Yahweh the foes of Rezin against him, and his enemies he stirred up:
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has raised Rezin's foes high against them \q and spurred on their enemies:

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised high the foes of Rezin against him, \q and his enemies {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stirred up:

R.10: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the enemies of King Rezin strong and sent them against Israel. \q He stirred up Israel's enemies to attack.

decisions.choice: the foes of Rezin: the enemies of Aram's king, set against Israel
decisions.reason: Rezin, king of Aram, was Israel's ally against Judah (7:1-2), so it is surprising to hear of his foes being raised against Israel. Assyria was Rezin's great foe: it took Damascus and killed Rezin in 732 BC, and then turned on Israel (2 Kings 16:9; 15:29). A change of one letter would give "the princes of Rezin", that is, Aram itself, and verse 11 names Aram among Israel's attackers. The Hebrew text as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: raised, stirred up: past blows; him and his are Israel
decisions.reason: The verbs tell what God has already done to Israel, the first of the blows in this poem. "Against him" and "his enemies" refer to Israel, named in verse 7.

decisions.choice: them, Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the plural for the people; Readable names Israel.

records.source: אֲרָ֣ם מִקֶּ֗דֶם וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ מֵֽאָח֔וֹר וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּכָל־פֶּ֑ה בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃
records.gloss: Aram from [the] east and Philistines from [the] west, and they devoured Israel with all [the] mouth. For all this not has turned back his anger, and still his hand [is] stretched out.
pieces: Aram from the east and the Philistines from the west \q have gulped Israel down with greedy mouths. \q In spite of all this, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is still stretched out.

L.11: Aram from the east and [the] Philistines from the west, \q and they devoured Israel with all [their] mouth. \q For all this {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and still {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [is] stretched out.

R.11: The Arameans came from the east, and the Philistines came from the west. \q They attacked Israel like hungry animals eating it up. \q But even after all this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is still angry. \q He is still ready to strike them with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.

decisions.choice: Aram and the Philistines: Israel's neighbors on either side
decisions.reason: Aram, with its capital at Damascus, lay to the north-east; the Philistine cities lay along the coast to the west. Israel was caught between them.

decisions.choice: with all the mouth: greedily, with open jaws
decisions.reason: The enemies are pictured as animals swallowing their prey whole.

decisions.choice: his anger has not turned back, his hand is still stretched out: the punishment is not over
decisions.reason: This refrain ends each stanza (9:16, 20; 10:4; also 5:25). God's anger has not yet turned away, and his hand is still raised to strike. The outstretched hand once saved Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:34); now it is against them.

decisions.choice: the LORD is still angry; he is still ready to strike them with his hand
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD, who sent the word (verse 7), and explains the stretched-out hand (m3).

decisions.choice: like hungry animals
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture of devouring a comparison (m2).

records.source: וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא־שָׁ֖ב עַד־הַמַּכֵּ֑הוּ וְאֶת־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And the people not has turned back to the [one] striking it, and Yahweh of hosts not they have sought.
pieces: And still the people have not come back to the one who struck them, \q nor gone looking for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.12: But the people have not turned back to the one who struck them, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts they have not sought.

R.12: But the people did not come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, even though {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had punished them. \q They did not ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies for help.

decisions.choice: turned back: returned to God, repented
decisions.reason: The same verb as in the refrain: God's anger has not turned back (verse 11) because the people have not turned back to him. Each blow was meant to bring them home (Amos 4:6-11).

decisions.choice: sought: turned to in worship and for help
decisions.reason: To seek God is to come to him for guidance and help. In 8:19 the people were consulting the dead instead of their God.

decisions.choice: the LORD, even though he had punished them
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who struck them (verse 11) and says what the striking was.

records.source: וַיַּכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֗ל רֹ֧אשׁ וְזָנָ֛ב כִּפָּ֥ה וְאַגְמ֖וֹן י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And cut off Yahweh from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, [in] day one.
pieces: So in one day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lopped off Israel's head and tail, the tall palm and the lowly rush.

L.13: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.

R.13: So in just one day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} cut off Israel's head and tail. He cut off both the tall palm branch and the short reed.

decisions.choice: head and tail, palm branch and reed: everyone, from the top to the bottom
decisions.reason: The two pairs mean the whole people, the highest and the lowest. The palm branch grows at the top of a tall tree; the reed grows in the marsh. 19:15 uses both pairs of Egypt. Verse 14 says who the head and tail are.

decisions.choice: cut off in one day: a sudden, complete blow
decisions.reason: The verb continues the past blows of verses 10-11; "in one day" stresses how sudden and complete it was.

records.source: זָקֵ֥ן וּנְשׂוּא־פָנִ֖ים ה֣וּא הָרֹ֑אשׁ וְנָבִ֥יא מֽוֹרֶה־שֶּׁ֖קֶר ה֥וּא הַזָּנָֽב׃
records.gloss: [An] elder and [one] lifted up of face, he [is] the head; and [a] prophet teaching falsehood, he [is] the tail.
pieces: The head means the old men and the people of high standing; \q the tail means the prophet whose teaching is false.

L.14: An elder and [one] lifted up of face, he [is] the head; \q and a prophet who teaches falsehood, he [is] the tail.

R.14: The head stands for the elders and the important people. \q The tail stands for the prophets whose teaching is not true.

decisions.choice: lifted up of face: honored, a person of rank
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to show him favor; a man "lifted of face" is respected and important (2 Kings 5:1, of Naaman; 3:3).

decisions.choice: the prophet who teaches lies is the tail
decisions.reason: The tail is the lowest, last part, and it wags behind. Prophets who told the people what they wanted to hear are condemned again in 28:7 and 30:10. The verse explains the picture of verse 13.

records.source: וַיִּֽהְי֛וּ מְאַשְּׁרֵ֥י הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה מַתְעִ֑ים וּמְאֻשָּׁרָ֖יו מְבֻלָּעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And were the guides of the people the this leading astray, and the [ones] guided by it [are] swallowed up.
pieces: Those who steer this people lead them off course, \q and those they steer are swallowed up.

L.15: And the guides of this people have been leading [them] astray, \q and those guided by them are swallowed up.

R.15: The leaders of these people lead them the wrong way. \q And the people who follow them are being destroyed.

decisions.choice: guides ... leading astray: the same charge as 3:12
decisions.reason: In 3:12 the same two words are paired: "your guides lead you astray". The word for guides comes from the root "go straight", so the guides who should lead straight lead the people off the path.

decisions.choice: swallowed up: destroyed, ruined
decisions.reason: The verb is "swallow", the same root as in 3:12 ("they swallow the way of your paths"). A word that sounds the same means "be confused", and some take it so here: "those who are led are confused".

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֨ן עַל־בַּחוּרָ֜יו לֹֽא־יִשְׂמַ֣ח׀אֲדֹנָ֗י וְאֶת־יְתֹמָ֤יו וְאֶת־אַלְמְנֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔ם כִּ֤י כֻלּוֹ֙ חָנֵ֣ף וּמֵרַ֔ע וְכָל־פֶּ֖ה דֹּבֵ֣ר נְבָלָ֑ה בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore over its young men not rejoices [the] Lord, and its fatherless and its widows not he has compassion on, for all of it [is] godless and evildoing, and every mouth [is] speaking disgraceful folly. For all this not has turned back his anger, and still his hand [is] stretched out.
pieces: That is why the Lord takes no delight in its young men and shows no mercy to its orphans and widows. \q Every one of them is godless and does evil, \q and every mouth speaks shameful folly. \q In spite of all this, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is still stretched out.

L.16: Therefore over its young men the Lord does not rejoice, and its orphans and its widows {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not pity; \q for all of it [is] godless and an evildoer, \q and every mouth speaks disgraceful folly. \q For all this {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and still {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [is] stretched out.

R.16: So the Lord is not pleased with their young men. He does not even feel sorry for their orphans and widows. \q That is because all the people are godless and wicked, and everyone says shameful things. \q But even after all this, the Lord is still angry. \q He is still ready to strike them with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.

decisions.choice: orphans and widows: even those God protects receive no pity
decisions.reason: Orphans and widows were under God's special care (1:17, 23; Deuteronomy 10:18). That even they receive no pity shows how complete the corruption is: the whole people shares in it.

decisions.choice: godless ... disgraceful folly: open contempt for God
decisions.reason: The first word describes someone who is profane, who treats God as of no account (33:14). The second is moral folly, an outrage, not mere foolishness (32:6).

decisions.choice: his anger has not turned back, his hand is still stretched out: the punishment is not over
decisions.reason: The refrain of 9:11, 16 and 20 (also 5:25 and 10:4; see the note at 9:11). Each blow is followed by the warning that more is coming.

decisions.choice: the Lord is still angry; he is still ready to strike them with his hand
decisions.reason: As at verse 11, Readable explains the refrain.

records.source: כִּֽי־בָעֲרָ֤ה כָאֵשׁ֙ רִשְׁעָ֔ה שָׁמִ֥יר וָשַׁ֖יִת תֹּאכֵ֑ל וַתִּצַּת֙ בְּסִֽבְכֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר וַיִּֽתְאַבְּכ֖וּ גֵּא֥וּת עָשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: For has burned like fire wickedness; thorns and briers it consumes, and it has kindled the thickets of the forest, and they have rolled up [in a] rising of smoke.
pieces: Wickedness blazes up like a fire. \q It eats through thorn and brier, \q catches the tangled undergrowth of the forest, \q and sends it whirling skyward in towering smoke.

L.17: For wickedness burns like fire; \q thorns and briers it devours, \q and it kindles the thickets of the forest, \q and they roll upward [in] a column of smoke.

R.17: The people's wickedness is like a spreading fire. It burns up thorns and weeds. \q It sets the bushes in the forest on fire, \q and thick smoke rises into the sky.

decisions.choice: wickedness burns like fire: sin brings its own ruin
decisions.reason: The people's evil is pictured as a fire that destroys them. Verse 18 says the land burns by the wrath of the LORD: the judgment is both the fruit of their sin and God's own act.

decisions.choice: thorns and briers: the pair used for a ruined land
decisions.reason: Isaiah uses this pair for the vineyard and the land left waste (5:6; 7:23-25) and for the fire that consumes Assyria (10:17).

decisions.choice: the people's wickedness
decisions.reason: Readable says whose wickedness it is.

records.source: בְּעֶבְרַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת נֶעְתַּ֣ם אָ֑רֶץ וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמַאֲכֹ֣לֶת אֵ֔שׁ אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֖יו לֹ֥א יַחְמֹֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: By [the] fury of Yahweh of hosts has been scorched [the] land, and was the people like fuel of fire; [a] man to his brother not they spare.
pieces: The fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has burned the land black, \q and the people have become like wood for the fire. \q No one spares even his own brother.

L.18: By the fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts the land has been scorched, \q and the people have become like fuel for fire; \q a man does not spare his brother.

R.18: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies was so angry that the land was burned up. \q The people became like wood in a fire. \q Nobody showed mercy, not even to their own relatives.

decisions.choice: has been scorched: burned up
decisions.reason: This verb occurs only here, and its sense is not certain. The picture of fire in verses 17-18 and the Septuagint ("burned up") support "scorched"; a related word in Arabic suggests "darkened" or "choked".

decisions.choice: a man does not spare his brother: civil strife
decisions.reason: Each one turns on his own people, as verses 19-20 go on to describe. In Israel's last years kings were murdered one after another (2 Kings 15:10, 14, 25, 30).

decisions.choice: their own relatives
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "brother" here: one's own people.

records.source: וַיִּגְזֹ֤ר עַל־יָמִין֙ וְרָעֵ֔ב וַיֹּ֥אכַל עַל־שְׂמֹ֖אול וְלֹ֣א שָׂבֵ֑עוּ אִ֥ישׁ בְּשַׂר־זְרֹע֖וֹ יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And he cut on [the] right and was hungry, and he ate on [the] left and not they were satisfied; each [the] flesh of his arm they eat.
pieces: They tear at food to their right and stay hungry; \q they gulp it down to their left and are never filled. \q Every one of them feeds on his own arm.

L.19: And [they] cut on the right but are hungry, \q and eat on the left but are not satisfied; \q each eats the flesh of his own arm.

R.19: They grab what they can on every side, but they are still hungry. \q They are never satisfied. \q They are destroying their own people, as if they were eating their own arms.

decisions.choice: cut on the right, eat on the left: grabbing on every side
decisions.reason: Right and left mean all around. The people seize whatever they can from those around them, yet hunger is never satisfied.

decisions.choice: eating the flesh of his own arm: tearing apart one's own people
decisions.reason: The arm is a person's strength and support, here one's own kin, the ones who should be one's help. Verse 20 explains: Manasseh against Ephraim. Jeremiah 19:9 speaks of people eating the flesh of their neighbors in the extremity of a siege, and the words may also be meant that way.

decisions.choice: They are destroying their own people, as if
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

records.source: מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אֶת־אֶפְרַ֗יִם וְאֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יַחְדָּ֥ו הֵ֖מָּה עַל־יְהוּדָ֑ה בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Manasseh Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they [are] against Judah. For all this not has turned back his anger, and still his hand [is] stretched out.
pieces: Manasseh preys on Ephraim, Ephraim on Manasseh, \q and both join hands against Judah. \q In spite of all this, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is still stretched out.

L.20: Manasseh [devours] Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; \q together they [are] against Judah. \q For all this {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and still {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [is] stretched out.

R.20: The tribe of Manasseh attacks the tribe of Ephraim, and Ephraim attacks Manasseh. \q Then both of them attack Judah together. \q But even after all this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is still angry. \q He is still ready to strike them with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.

decisions.choice: Manasseh and Ephraim against each other, and both against Judah
decisions.reason: Manasseh and Ephraim were the two sons of Joseph (Genesis 48) and the leading tribes of the north. Brother tribes fought each other, yet joined to attack Judah, their brother kingdom, as Israel did with Aram in 734 BC (7:1-6; 2 Kings 16:5).

decisions.choice: Manasseh [devours] Ephraim: the verb is understood from verse 19
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the names side by side with no verb; the eating of verse 19 is carried over.

decisions.choice: his anger has not turned back, his hand is still stretched out: the punishment is not over
decisions.reason: The refrain of 9:11, 16 and 20 (also 5:25 and 10:4; see the note at 9:11). Each blow is followed by the warning that more is coming.

decisions.choice: the LORD is still angry; he is still ready to strike them with his hand
decisions.reason: As at verse 11, Readable explains the refrain.
